contexts.text: The sword devouring () = the vastation of truth.
To catch the prey, and to devour men () = to destroy truths and goods.
To devour the little book () = to acknowledge it.
To devour (the child of the woman) () = to extinguish it.
The one seemed to devour the other...
It appeared as if they devoured it...
The devouring (of the little book) = exploration.

To devour or eat up = to conjoin and appropriate to one's self; and as the Word is conjoined with man through reading and perception, to devour or eat up = to read and perceive. The reason to devour, here, also = to explore, is because (of what follows).
I devoured it = exploration... To devour or eat it = to receive, perceive, and appropriate to one's self; thus, also, to explore.
To devour their enemies () = that they will perish through the falsities of evil.
To devour (the child of the woman) = to destroy. Explained.
That to devour and to eat up = to destroy, when they are said of wild beasts. Illustrated.
To sacrifice sons and daughters to be devoured () = to destroy and consume all the truths and goods of the Church.
The sword of Jehovah devouring () = falsity destroying.
